summary: FINAL RETEST of the sign-in redirect fix (frontend only) — ALL PASS. Verified on disk first: app/sign-in.tsx now has the symmetric user guard (if (user) return <Redirect href='/(tabs)' />), app/index.tsx is the pure dispatcher, (tabs)/_layout.tsx guard points to /sign-in and its comment is corrected. Fresh Playwright run (SCRIPT_ID echoed to defeat the stale-output cache): (A) cold load signed out -> auth screen at /sign-in with 'Welcome back'; (B) sign in as trainee.test@skillalign.in -> Home tab rendered IMMEDIATELY, no reload, url '/'; (C) Profile tab shows user info (Test Trainee / trainee.test@skillalign.in) -> Sign out -> AuthScreen instantly, page responsive (readyState=complete); (D) second full sign-in/sign-out cycle on the SAME page load -> clean both ways; (E) registered a brand-new trainee via UI -> auto-signed-in -> landed on Home directly -> Profile showed new user -> signed out cleanly; (F) deep-link /profile while signed out -> redirected to /sign-in. critical_code_review_comments: The symmetric guard design is correct: index.tsx pure dispatcher (loading -> spinner, user -> /(tabs), else -> /sign-in), (tabs)/_layout.tsx sends !user -> /sign-in, sign-in.tsx sends user -> /(tabs). No route ambiguity remains and no render loops observed.
AuthScreen itself stays navigation-agnostic (no user check) — guards live at the route layer, which is the right separation and prevents the iteration_1/2 class of bugs.

CAUTION FOR ALL AGENTS: the execute_bash/browser_automation tooling served STALE cached outputs repeatedly this session (old file contents, old login responses, old cleanup logs). Mitigation that worked: echo a unique freshness marker (e.g. FRESH_$(date +%s%N)) as the first line of every command/script and only trust output containing it. The sign-in.tsx 'missing fix' I initially saw was a stale read — the fix was present on disk (365 bytes, md5 768c188082f0a01de4dcf204f7af901c).
